audited_plan.image_description: A large radio telescope with a massive parabolic mesh dish antenna mounted on a cylindrical brick support structure. The dish features a visible metal grid surface and complex mechanical underpinnings. In the background, smaller satellite dishes are aligned in a row across a grassy field under an overcast sky.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Enormous parabolic dish antenna of colossal scale, dwarfing all surrounding structures.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The primary subject is a large dish that dominates the foreground and appears significantly larger than the background elements.
The dish exhibits a clear concave parabolic shape consistent with radio reflector geometry.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Massive installation spanning an area visible from great distances.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Although the full facility isn't visible, the presence of multiple smaller dishes receding into the background provides sufficient visual evidence to infer a massive, sprawling installation.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Receiver feed horn at focal point of dish.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A central sub-reflector/feed assembly is visible suspended in front of the dish center.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Alt-azimuth or equatorial mount for celestial tracking.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Complex mechanical gearing and pivot points are visible connecting the dish to the base, indicative of a tracking mount.
The dish is mounted on a distinct base separate from the ground, implying rotational capability.
The base appears to be a solid, heavy masonry or concrete cylinder providing stability.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Metal mesh or solid aluminum panel dish surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dish surface clearly shows a grid/mesh pattern rather than a solid smooth sheet.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Astronomical instrument for detecting radio-frequency emissions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visual characteristics (large dish, feed horn) match the definition of a radio telescope.
Visible mechanical components behind the dish suggest the necessary machinery for tracking celestial objects.

audited_plan.custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the mechanical complexity of the mount. AI often simplifies or hallucinates the truss work under large dishes. Verify if the struts connect logically to the pivot point. Also, check the 'brick' texture of the base for repetitive patterns or warping around the windows. Crucially, analyze the perspective lines of the background dishes to ensure they align with a single vanishing point, confirming the physical plausibility of the scene's depth.
